chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl, and 'Abdullah al-Hajjāl, from Thal'abah ibn Maymūn, from Zurārah, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the Hajar al-Aswad (the Stone), is there anything of the Ka'bah in it? He said, 'No, not even the thickness of a nail.'
ai.seo_question: Is the Hajar al-Aswad part of the Ka'bah's structure?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the nature of the Hajar al-Aswad by stating it is not a fragment of the Ka'bah's structure, emphasizing its distinct ontological status. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the specific rulings regarding the stone's sanctity and the expiation (kaffarah) for accidentally damaging it while in the state of ihram.
